newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: French Guiana ravaged by AIDS.
newsitem.headline: French Guiana ravaged by AIDS.

text.p: French Guiana, which a decade ago had the world's highest AIDS rate, continues to be ravaged by the disease with one of the western hemisphere's highest infection rates, experts said on Sunday.
One person in every 70 could be infected with the HIV virus that causes AIDS in the equatorial French overseas territory of 150,000 on the northeast coast of South America, the AIDES group said.
"There are 561 people with full-blown AIDS...about one person in 250," said Doctor Genevieve Simart of AIDES on local state-owned radio.

"As for persons HIV positive, we can only estimate. Certain markers lead us to say that there are between 1,000 and 1,500 people infected if we are being very optimistic -- 2,000 to 2,500 people infected if we are more pessimistic, which gives a rate of one person for 70. This is enormous," Simart said.
Officials said AIDS infection in French Guiana was five times worse than in mainland France. They said most cases were heterosexually transmitted and in the 30-49 age group.
French Guiana and the French Caribbean islands also led France for children infected with the HIV virus.
French Guiana had the world's highest AIDS rates in the mid- 1980's when statistics for the disease became public.

The Geneva-based World Health Organisation (WHO) estimates that nearly 28 million people have been infected worldwide with HIV since the start of the epidemic 15 years ago. An additional 26 million may be infected by the year 2000.
